# AP-BAG-001 Staff Baggage Handling and Escalation

## 1. Purpose and Scope  
This policy establishes procedures for the handling of checked baggage throughout the airport's baggage handling system. It outlines the responsibilities of staff involved in the movement and management of baggage, ensuring compliance with safety, security, and operational standards. The policy applies to all baggage handlers, baggage duty supervisors, and ramp leads. It ensures that baggage is processed efficiently and that any incidents or irregularities are addressed in a timely and consistent manner. This policy supports the safe and secure transportation of baggage and aligns with the airport's broader operational and security objectives.

## 2. Roles and Responsibilities  
The baggage handler is responsible for the safe and efficient movement of baggage between the check-in belts, baggage make-up area, and aircraft loading zones. The baggage duty supervisor oversees the operations of baggage handlers and ensures adherence to handling standards. The ramp lead is responsible for coordinating baggage operations with aircraft crews and ensuring that all baggage is loaded and secured in accordance with safety protocols. All staff must follow established procedures, report any issues promptly, and maintain clear communication to ensure the smooth operation of the baggage handling process.

## 3. Handling Standards  
Baggage handlers must ensure that all baggage is properly tagged, loaded, and secured during the handling process. Bag tags must be affixed correctly to ensure accurate identification and tracking. Heavy bags must be handled with care to prevent damage or injury. Fragile items should be clearly marked and handled with extra caution to avoid breakage. All baggage must be loaded in accordance with aircraft loading guidelines and weight distribution requirements. Staff must inspect baggage for any signs of damage or tampering before and after handling to ensure the integrity of the baggage and the safety of the operation.

## 4. Baggage Incident Escalation  
When a baggage handler finds a damaged, leaking, or unattended checked bag in the baggage make-up area, the handler must escalate the incident to the Baggage Duty Supervisor within 30 minutes of discovery and must report it under AP-INC-002. All incidents must be documented in the incident log and reported to the appropriate supervisory personnel. If a baggage handler identifies an issue that cannot be resolved independently, they must escalate the matter to the Baggage Duty Supervisor for further action. The Baggage Duty Supervisor is responsible for ensuring that all incidents are investigated and resolved in accordance with established procedures. Escalation ensures that potential risks are addressed promptly and that the integrity of the baggage handling process is maintained.

## 5. Restricted Items Found in Baggage  
If a restricted item is found in a bag during the baggage handling process, the baggage handler must not proceed with further handling of the bag until it is approved or removed under the restricted-items approval procedure in AP-SEC-003. The handler must secure the bag and notify the Baggage Duty Supervisor immediately. The Baggage Duty Supervisor is responsible for initiating the restricted-items approval process and ensuring that the bag is either approved for transport or removed in accordance with applicable regulations. All staff must be aware of the procedures for identifying and handling restricted items to ensure compliance with security and safety standards.

## 6. Records and Review  
All baggage incidents must be recorded in the incident log, which is maintained by the Baggage Duty Supervisor. The log must include details such as the time of discovery, the nature of the incident, and the actions taken. The incident log is reviewed annually to assess the effectiveness of the baggage handling procedures and to identify any areas for improvement. The Baggage Duty Supervisor is responsible for ensuring that the log is accurate and up to date. Annual review of this policy ensures that it remains relevant and effective in supporting the safe and secure handling of baggage.
